title: Beyond Reconstruction Error: Analytical and Data-Driven Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.25820v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Discrete action tokenization is central to autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models, yet action representations are often evaluated primarily through reconstruction fidelity. We ask which representation properties actually matter for closed-loop control by comparing fixed analytical, data-driven linear, and nonlinear neural representations under a unified tokenization interface. Across rate-distortion analysis, sequence-modeling diagnostics, and 3,500 LIBERO rollouts, representation rankings change with the evaluation criterion. PCA achieves lower nominal reconstruction error than Temporal-DCT, but produces less predictable token sequences and 3.0 percentage points lower mean seen-task success across three policy-training seeds, with the policy ordering reversing in one seed. In a matched seed-42 ablation, an autoencoder further reduces reconstruction error yet does not yield the strongest policy and exhibits greater sensitiv

translated_title: 超越重构误差：面向自回归视觉-语言-动作模型的分析式与数据驱动动作分词方法
translated_abstract: 离散动作分词是自回归视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型的核心，然而动作表示的评估往往主要依据重构保真度。我们探究了哪些表示性质对闭环控制真正重要，方法是在统一的分词接口下比较固定解析式表示、数据驱动线性表示与非线性神经表示。通过率-失真分析、序列建模诊断以及3,500次LIBERO仿真测试，我们发现表示的排名会随评估准则而变化。PCA的名义重构误差虽低于Temporal-DCT，但其生成的词元序列可预测性更差，且在三个策略训练随机种子下，已见任务的平均成功率低3.0个百分点，其中一个种子的策略排序甚至发生逆转。在匹配的seed-42消融实验中，自编码器进一步降低了重构误差，却并未带来最强的策略表现，并且表现出更大的敏感性……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文超越以重构误差评估动作表示的传统做法，在统一分词接口下系统比较解析式与数据驱动的动作分词方法，发现更低的重构误差并不对应更好的闭环控制性能，词元序列的可预测性才是决定自回归VLA模型策略成功率的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that reconstruction error is not a reliable proxy for action representation quality in autoregressive VLA models: under a unified tokenization interface, representations with lower reconstruction error (e.g., PCA, autoencoders) yield less predictable token sequences and worse closed-loop control success, showing that token sequence predictability matters more than reconstruction fidelity.
